text:
Anjali: Heads-up — the deploy window at 01:00 UTC includes API, runtime, console, and router. I want a quick alignment on dependency contracts and pin strategy.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled at 01:00 UTC. Automated preflight will run at 00:40. Tag: release/v2.9.1.

Kevin: Quick Q — are we pinning router->runtime to v2.9.1 or allowing runtime to roll while router stays on v2.9.0? I want to avoid mixed KV protocol changes.

Maria: Runtime has a small header-split change (opt-in). If router is still v2.9.0 it will ignore new header flags, safe by default. But API schema requires the new header for the new quota flow.

Anjali: Decision needed: pin API+runtime together, console and router can be staggered? If API requires header we must coordinate router within the same window or opt API feature flag off.

Jen: My vote is pin API+runtime for the first wave, stagger console then router 30m later. Console can tolerate partial runtime mismatch, router is more sensitive for routing contracts.

Sam: +1. Also suggest we enable the runtime backward-compat check in preflight: run smoke with router v2.9.0 docker image against runtime v2.9.1 and assert no 4xx regressions.

deploy-bot: Preflight checklist: 1) integration smoke (api->runtime->router) 2) canary 5% for 15m 3) metric gates: p50 latency, error_rate <= 0.5% 4) rollback hook enabled.

Kevin: If we pin API+runtime, we should register a temporary fallback: route to runtime v2.9.0 if canary errors exceed threshold. Is that supported by the routing policy?

Maria: Yes — we have a routing-policy flag: "fallback_candidates: [v2.9.0, v2.8.x]". Need to ensure console respects header flag to avoid UI churn.

Anjali: Procedural:
- API/runtime pinned to v2.9.1 (no partial rollout)
- Console staggered at +30m if metrics good
- Router staggered at +60m with compatibility smoke first
- Rollback criteria: any 5m window with error_rate > 1% or token latency p90 > 3s

Jen: I'll update release notes and include the opt-out env var for the header feature for Console teams.

Sam: For the preflight smoke, use this command to run the scenario locally:
```
./deploy/tools/smoke --topology api:local,runtime:v2.9.1,router:v2.9.0 --tests smoke_quota_flow
```

Kevin: Thanks — I'll queue the compatibility run and post results. If we see header-related 4xx we'll abort and toggle API feature flag off.

deploy-bot: Canary started at 01:00 UTC -> instances: 12 -> traffic: 5%

Sam: Canary results: 01:10 UTC - no increased 4xx; p50 latency +30ms; error_rate 0.12%. Good to proceed with staged rollout.

Anjali: Rolling API/runtime to 100% now. Console at +30m. Router at +60m pending a router-canary smoke.

Maria: Router-canary smoke scheduled for 01:55 UTC. Running with a mirrored traffic slice.

Kevin: Router-canary shows a stray 502 spike at 02:02 UTC (15s window) — tracing shows an older sidecar eviction race. Not directly header related.

Jen: Is that a hard stop? Can we mitigate by increasing graceful eviction window on router sidecars before rolling out router globally?

Sam: Yes — quick mitigation: bump ENV ROUTER_SIDECAR_GRACE=12s and retry canary. I can stage that immediately and re-run smoke.

deploy-bot: Canary redeployed with ROUTER_SIDECAR_GRACE=12s -> monitoring 02:12 UTC.

Maria: Second canary steady. No 5xx, latencies nominal. Recommend proceeding with router staggered rollout.

Anjali: Final call: proceed. Release notes: include upgrade matrix, rollback steps, and the ENV knob for rollback mitigation.

Jen: Added release note snippet to PR #4821 and pinged Console lead for the opt-out instruction.

Kevin: I'll watch the post-rollout dashboard and be ready to flip the routing fallback to v2.9.0 if needed.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete at 02:25 UTC. All services at v2.9.1 (router rolled at 02:20). No active alerts. :tada:

Anjali: Great work, team. Postmortem action item: add automated compatibility smoke to preflight for header-schema changes.

Sam: Filing a short RFC for automated header-compat checks this afternoon.

Jen: Thanks everyone.
